head: They tried to sell
snowboards.
slides.sub: The software they built to do it became the business.

image.label: A snowboard leaning against a desk with a glowing laptop
image.brief: 2000년대 중반 캐나다의 작은 아파트. 창가에 기대 세운 스노보드와 코드가 떠 있는 노트북 화면. 창밖은 눈 내리는 겨울 밤. 브랜드 로고 없음.

head: A small shop
with no store.
body: In 2004, in Ottawa, Canada, a young German programmer named Tobias Lütke and his partner Scott Lake wanted to sell snowboards online.
They called the shop Snowdevil. First, they needed a website where people could actually buy.

image.label: Snowboards stacked in a small apartment
image.brief: 2004년 오타와의 좁은 아파트 한쪽에 쌓인 스노보드 상자들. 겨울 오후의 차가운 햇빛. 인물은 뒷모습 실루엣으로만.

head: The tools for selling online
were painful.
body: The e-commerce software they tried was clunky, expensive or hard to change. It felt built for big retailers, not for a tiny shop run by two people.
Lütke was a programmer. So he decided to write his own.

image.label: A frustrated person staring at a cluttered admin screen
image.brief: 복잡한 2000년대 관리자 화면 앞에서 머리를 감싼 사람의 실루엣. 회색빛 UI, 얼굴은 보이지 않게.

head: He built the store
from scratch.
body: Lütke used Ruby on Rails, a new web framework at the time, to build Snowdevil's online store himself.
The snowboards sold modestly. But the store software was clean, fast and easy to run. In a story often told, they realized the software was worth more than the boards.

image.label: Lines of code on a screen late at night
image.brief: 밤늦은 책상 위 모니터에 가득한 코드. 옆에 식은 커피잔. 따뜻한 스탠드 조명.

head: Your side project is
better than your shop.
body: Other small sellers have the same problem you did. Your store software solves it. What do you do next?

options.text: Keep focusing on snowboards and use the software as your edge
options.feedback: Your shop gets a better website than rivals. But you stay a small seller in a seasonal, crowded market. Keep swiping.

options.text: Turn it into a product any seller can sign up for and run alone
options.feedback: You leave the shop behind and bet on a market that barely exists yet. Keep swiping.

options.text: Build custom stores for other shops as a paid service
options.feedback: It brings cash quickly, but every client means more hours of your own work. Keep swiping.

image.label: A crossroads sign in snow, one arrow to a shop, one to a laptop
image.brief: 눈 덮인 갈림길 표지판. 한쪽은 스노보드 가게, 다른 쪽은 노트북을 가리키는 화살표. 단순하고 상징적인 일러스트.

head: They stopped selling boards.
They sold the store.
body: In 2006 they launched Shopify: a tool that let anyone open an online store without writing code, for a monthly fee.
The customer wasn't a snowboarder anymore. It was every small seller who had hit the same wall Snowdevil had.

image.label: Many small shop windows glowing on a laptop screen
image.brief: 노트북 화면 속에 작은 온라인 가게 창들이 여러 개 켜져 있는 장면. 의류, 커피, 수공예품 등 다양한 업종. 실제 로고 없음.

head: Slow at first.
Then it compounded.
body: Growth was slow in the early years. By 2008, Lütke had become CEO. In 2009, Shopify opened an app store so outside developers could add features for merchants.
Every new merchant paid every month, and many stayed as their own businesses grew.

image.label: A small office with a whiteboard full of merchant growth notes
image.brief: 2000년대 후반 오타와의 작은 사무실. 화이트보드에 성장 그래프 낙서. 인물은 실루엣으로.

slides.label: merchants on Shopify when it went public in 2015, according to its filing
body: In May 2015, the company that began as a snowboard shop listed its shares in New York and Toronto.

image.label: A trading floor screen with an abstract rising chart
image.brief: 2015년 증권거래소 분위기의 큰 화면에 추상적인 상승 그래프. 실제 거래소 로고나 티커 디자인은 쓰지 않음.

head: They felt the pain
before they sold the fix.
body: Lütke didn't start by guessing what merchants needed. He was a merchant, stuck with bad tools, and solved his own problem first.
Then they pivoted from the product they sold to the tool they built, and charged for it as a monthly subscription that grew with their customers.

image.label: A snowboard turning into a shopping cart icon
image.brief: 스노보드 실루엣이 장바구니 아이콘으로 서서히 변하는 그래픽. 미니멀한 톤.

head: Your workaround might be
someone else's product.
body: The tool you built to fix your own problem may matter more than the business you built it for.
**Try it today:** list one process or tool your team made because nothing on the market worked. Who else might pay for it?

image.label: A single snowboard on a snowy hill at sunrise
image.brief: 해 뜨는 눈 덮인 언덕 위에 꽂힌 스노보드 한 장. 조용하고 희망적인 톤.

factChecks.note: Snowdevil의 창업 시기(2004년), 장소(캐나다 오타와), 창업자 Tobias Lütke·Scott Lake(및 Daniel Weinand)는 Shopify 공식 연혁과 주요 언론 보도로 확인하세요. 카드에는 Lütke와 Scott Lake만 언급했습니다.
기존 이커머스 소프트웨어에 실망해 Lütke가 Ruby on Rails로 직접 스토어를 만들었다는 이야기는 Lütke 본인의 여러 인터뷰에 나옵니다. 소프트웨어가 스노보드보다 가치 있다고 깨달았다는 부분은 "a story often told"로 표시했습니다.
Shopify 플랫폼 정식 출시 연도(2006년)와 월 구독료 모델은 Shopify 공식 연혁으로 확인하세요.
Shopify App Store 출시(2009년)와 Lütke의 CEO 취임(2008년 무렵)은 공식 연혁과 당시 보도로 확인하세요. 카드에서 CEO 취임 연도는 "by 2008"로만 적었습니다.
2015년 5월 NYSE·TSX 상장은 회사 발표와 당시 Reuters 등 보도 기준입니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2015년 5월 21일 NYSE·TSX 상장, 주당 17달러 확인.

"150,000곳 이상 판매자"는 2015년 상장 서류(F-1, 2015년 초 기준 약 16만 곳 이상) 기준 근사치입니다. 카드에는 "more than 150,000"와 "according to its filing"으로 적었습니다. 정확한 수치와 기준일을 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 상장 완료 시점 16만 5천 개 이상 사업체 확인(회사 발표). '15만 이상' 표현은 보수적.
